items.title: The Duskbloods closed network test had more applicants than Elden Ring Nightreign despite being a Switch 2 exclusive, FromSoftware lead reveals
items.content:
Nightreign being multi-platform didn't give it the edge here

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Duskbloods might be a Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive game, but one FromSoftware lead says that more fans signed up for its closed network test than they did for the multi-platform Elden Ring Nightreign .

Between Elden Ring Nightreign's release last year and The Duskbloods coming this year, FromSoftware is truly in its multiplayer era right now. It's not that the studio is changing its trajectory to ditch single-player games , mind you, as boss Hidetaka Miyazaki says, "both of those ideas just coincided with being multiplayer games. It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward."

Perhaps, though, the success of last year's co-op, roguelike-flavored souls game left more folks excited to see what the studio was cooking up with The Duskbloods. In an interview with Famitsu (translated by GamesRadar+), FromSoftware producer Yasuhiro Kitao reveals that the number of applications for the Switch 2 game's closed network test exceeded that for Nightreign's. "We were really surprised," he notes.

It is surprising, given that the Switch 2 is a single platform – and one that only just launched last year – it's bound to have a smaller installed base than the combined force of PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, and Xbox One, as Nightreign has. Kitao acknowledges this, saying that FromSoftware questions if there really will be more Duskbloods players come launch, and noting that it'll probably be Nightreign that comes out on top.

Even so, it's a positive early sign for The Duskbloods. After all, multiplayer-focused games live and die by how many players they have – their popularity is usually what makes the difference between something being supported for years to come, or being quietly shelved.

items.title: George R. R. Martin's New Dark Fantasy Is Already Bigger Than Lord of the Rings in Every Way
items.summary: A new video game adaptation is coming to the screen, and it's already going to be bigger than Lord of the Rings.
items.content:
Sean Astin as Samwise Gamee in The Lord of the Rings: The Return fo the King Image via New Line/courtesy Everett Collection By Fawzia Khan Published Aug 23, 2026, 5:30 PM EDT Fawzia Khan is a writer, photographer, and creative producer. She holds a bachelor's degree in journalism, and has worked extensively in the entertainment industry. She has previously worked at the photo desk at GQ Magazine. You can read her work in Elle Magazine, ScreenRant, The Wire, CLAD, Times of India, and DSSC. Her debut romance novel, part of a larger series, is currently in the works. Sign in to your CBR account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Consider what it takes for a video game to become a cultural phenomenon, and that means more than just being commercially successful. Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R.R. Martin's Elden Ring was released in February 2022 and has fast become the kind of game that rewires how people talk about the entire medium. It sold 12 million copies in eighteen days, and global sales reached 30 million by April 2025. Then consider that A24 has committed over $100 million to turning the phenomenon that is Elden Ring into a film, and has hired the writer-director of Ex Machina and Civil War to make it.

The cast of the upcoming movie includes Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, Ben Whishaw, Tom Burke, Nick Offerman, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Emma Laird, and Peter Serafinowicz. It is all set to be one of the most major gaming cinema events, especially since it has been given a release date that lands in the same March theatrical window that Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring once used to announce a new era of fantasy cinema. Whatever Elden Ring might be, it is arriving with the full weight of a cultural reckoning behind it.

The premise of Elden Ring sounds, in summary, almost impossibly dense. The titular artefact is one of supreme cosmic significance, and it has been shattered when the game begins. The Erdtree, the source of grace that sustains the world, has been corrupted, and the demigod children of Queen Marika the Eternal have gone to war over the Ring's fragments. In doing so, they have broken the Lands Between, which is the game's central realm, into a wasteland of warring factions, ancient curses, and creatures twisted by millennia of conflict.

The player enters as Tarnished, a warrior stripped of grace and returned from beyond death, tasked with gathering the Great Runes scattered across the Lands Between and repairing the Elden Ring to become Elden Lord.

What makes this translatable to film, despite its complexity, is that the game's surface mythology sits atop an emotional architecture that is straightforward and deeply human. This is a story about a world broken by the ambitions of people in power, and about one person navigating the wreckage of that breakage.

Martin's fingerprints are most visible in the political and genealogical density of the world's history: the tragedy of Queen Marika, the betrayal of Godfrey the first Elden Lord, the deeply Martin-esque irony that virtually every figure of power in the Lands Between has been destroyed by the very thing they fought to possess.

This is the author who spent 30 years building a world in which good intentions and terrible consequences occupy the same characters, and Elden Ring's mythology reflects that same sensibility, albeit in a different skin. Alex Garland has written and directed the cinematic adaptation, and has described himself as a genuine fan of FromSoftware's work.

Image via FromSoftware The Lord of the Rings comparison is one that any new fantasy epic invites and most cannot survive, because Tolkien's films set a standard not just for quality, but of cultural percolation that almost nothing in the genre has matched in 25 years. That said, the Elden Ring film arrives with advantages that Jackson's trilogy did not have, and with a source material whose footprint within its audience is arguably already larger.

Thirty million copies sold make Elden Ring one of the bestselling games of the modern era, and the game's audience is not passive consumers but active, deeply invested participants who have spent hundreds of hours inside the Lands Between. They have theorized the lore, mapped its geography, and built a community of interpretation around its deliberately fragmented storytelling.

This is an audience that does not need to be introduced to the world like newbies. It needs the world rendered in a new medium at a level of craft that justifies the translation. This is a different challenge from what Jackson faced in 2001, when most of his audience was encountering Middle-earth for the first time. It is, in some ways, a harder one: the expectations are more specific, the knowledge is deeper, and the tolerance for compromise is lower.

The A24 dimension adds another layer that no previous fantasy blockbuster has had. A24 is not a studio that makes $100 million movies as a routine commercial exercise. Every major investment they have made, from Hereditary to Everything Everywhere All At Once to the upcoming Death Stranding , has been a deliberate creative bet on a filmmaker with a specific vision for specific material.

Their involvement in Elden Ring signals that this is not an IP extraction exercise but a real attempt to make a great film from great material, which is the only approach that has any chance of satisfying the thirty million people who already love the source material.

Martin's role as producer rather than screenwriter is also meaningful. He has been direct about his philosophy of adaptation: the best translations of his work involve understanding what the source material is doing thematically rather than reproducing its plot. His presence on this production without the weight of also writing the screenplay gives Garland the creative latitude that Game of Thrones' best seasons had and its worst seasons lost. Martin built the world, and Garland can now build the movie.

The IMAX commitment is the final piece of this picture, and it is not incidental. Shooting Elden Ring for IMAX means the Lands Between will be rendered at a scale and resolution that makes the theatrical experience irreplaceable. Jackson understood that some stories were meant to be told on the biggest screen possible back in 2001, and Garland and A24 understand it in 2028 for Elden Ring. That understanding, more than any other casting decision or plot detail, is what separates a landmark fantasy film from an expensive one.

items.title: Elden Ring Tops Switch 2 eShop Chart
items.summary: Elden Ring reaches No. 1 on the Switch 2 eShop all-games chart through pre-loads, while DayZ leads the download-only rankings.
items.content:
Elden Ring has reached No. 1 on the Nintendo Switch 2 eShop all-games chart for the week of August 23, 2026, despite not yet being available. Pre-loads recently began, and that activity was enough to place the game ahead of Splatoon Raiders and Mario Kart World , according to Nintendo Everything .

The chart places Elden Ring first while the game remains in its pre-load period. Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 , another title launching next week, is also available for pre-load and ranks No. 6.

Beyond the top 10, Lies of P is No. 11, while The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion Remastered Deluxe Edition is No. 12. Zelda: Breath of the Wild – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition ranks No. 13, and The Lord of the Rings: War in the North – Legacy Edition is No. 14.

Starsand Island debuts at No. 18. Other entries in the top 30 include Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds at No. 19, Pokemon Legends: Z-A – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition at No. 20, Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition at No. 22, and Final Fantasy 14 at No. 23.

The download-only chart has a different leader, with DayZ taking the No. 1 position after ranking seventh on the all-games chart. Lies of P is second, followed by The Lord of the Rings: War in the North – Legacy Edition in third.

Further down that list, Deltarune is No. 11, Stardew Valley – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is No. 13, and Hollow Knight: Silksong – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is No. 20.

Zelda: Breath of the Wild – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition and Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition also appear on the all-games list, at Nos. 13 and 22 respectively. The chart additionally includes Final Fantasy 14 Complete Edition at No. 26, Mario Tennis Fever at No. 28, Yoshi and the Mysterious Book at No. 29, and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment at No. 30.

items.title: RPGs Coming This Week, August 23–29, 2026 – Strategy, Souls-Likes, and Small Rodents
items.summary: It's been a bit of a journey, but Elden Ring finally lands on Switch 2 this week. Joining it are two decidedly different strategy games, one a bit lesser
items.content:
It’s been a bit of a journey , but Elden Ring finally lands on Switch 2 this week. Joining it are two decidedly different strategy games, one a bit lesser known than the other one set in a galaxy far, far away. Also, mice! And squirrels. (Look, you try writing these intros every week and see how easy it is to sum up a week with an anime SRPG, pixel rodents, alongside the likes of Star Wars , The Lands Between, and a Peabody Award-winning adventure.)

Publisher Happinet returns with a new entry in the cult classic SRPG series, Brigandine Abyss . Developed by newcomer to the franchise Adglobe , Abyss ditches the unique fantasy art style (designed by Raita Kazama ) employed by the previous entry, Legend of Runersia , and instead opts for more familiar modern fantasy anime stylings. The gameplay is still the series’ characteristic blend of Grand Strategy map conquering (think Civilization or Nobunaga’s Ambition ) and turn-based tactical RPG combat on hex-grid battlefields. Although I found the game paled in comparison to prior entries, Abyss offers an engaging Mission Mode to test your strategic thinking with a wide variety of objectives, and a lovely, bombastic soundtrack by composer Rei Kondoh . If training up squads of monster units to conquer a big fantasy map appeals to you, it’s worth a look.

Four words: “ XCOM meets Star Wars .” Sound interesting? Search your feelings, you know it to be true. Star Wars Zero Company is a joint effort between Respawn Entertainment (behind the recent hits Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order and Jedi: Survivor , as well as Apex Legends ) and Bit Reactor, a new studio formed from many transplants from Firaxis Games (the XCOM series, the Civilization series, Marvel’s Midnight Suns ). In XCOM: Enemy Unknown fashion, Star Wars Zero Company is a turn-based tactics game where you command a customizable squadron of mercenaries made up of droids and various alien species.

Despite running parallel with the Clone Wars era, Zero Company features a shady new threat: the Infinite Coil cult, who plan on releasing a dark plague on the galaxy. Building and conversing with your crew seems to be a big focus, which will make it doubly painful when your allies fall prey to the game’s potential permadeath state. Meesa very interested. RPGFan’s Scott Clay wrote a preview and created an extensive hands-on video preview for the game on our YouTube channel.

At last, the expansive world of The Lands Between, able to fit in your (massive Switch 2-sized) pocket. Elden Ring Tarnished Edition bundles the jaw-dropping open world Souls-like Elden Ring with its ginormous, imposing expansion Shadow of the Erdtree , along with a small handful of bells and whistles in the form of four new armour sets, three skins for your mount, Torrent, and two new starting classes. (For returning players, these features will be sold separately in a DLC “Tarnished Pack”.)

If you’ve yet to try Elden Ring , I’m tempted to call it one of the greatest open-world games and one of the greatest action RPGs of all time, and I don’t think I’m alone in that (Editor’s Interjection: You aren’t alone, Matt; see Jerry’s stellar review !). Developer FromSoftware took a huge world and packed it wall to wall with challenging bosses, nightmarish horrors, and awe-inducing vistas that somehow feel incredibly bespoke. Elden Ring doesn’t hold your hand so much as it throttles you by the neck, but the adversity it presents will harden you into a powerful adventurer, whether solo or via online co-op. It’s a plunge into an abyss well worth taking.

After launching on PC in November 2023, indie RPG Small Saga surprisingly dropped last week on the Nintendo Switch. A charming little game that appears heavily influenced by Bryan Jacques’ anthropomorphised animal fantasy series Redwall , you inhabit the role of a mouse and his woodland companions (moles, squirrels, etc.) seeking revenge against the god who stole his tail. The game has a traditional turn-based combat system, though the animal characters use a myriad of repurposed human knick-knacks in battle (a pencil, a lighter, a pocket knife) to get the most out of its diminutive setting. I have to admit this one passed me by on release, but I’m eager to give it a try.

1000xRESIST dropped on Switch 2 in the middle of the week, so we wanted to be sure to include it here. The short version is that this is a sci-fi adventure set 1000 years in the future where an alien disease has wiped out most of humanity… and frankly, it seems like the kind of game that may be best going in with as little context as possible. And I partially say this because I just got it myself, thanks to the 40% launch discount on the Nintendo eShop .

But by now you’ve probably heard about it, whether from our Games of the Year 2025 feature , or places like RPGFan alumni Alana Hagues’ review at Nintendo Life , or when developers Sunset Visitor won a Peabody Award , and was nominated for a Hugo Award (though the latter ultimately went to Caves of Qud , which our own Aleks Franiczek adored ). The key things to note about the new Switch 2 Edition is that it improves the visuals, resolution, and framerate over the Switch 1 version, allowing players to experience the game as intended. And if you do have it on Switch 1, the Switch 2 Edition is a free upgrade. I love it when that happens.

Finally, to coincide with this announcement, Fangamer revealed a pair of physical editions for Switch 1/2 and PS5, with a host of extra items packed in, such as holographic buttons, unique cover art, a poster, trading cards, and more. They are up for preorder now on the Fangamer website , and will ship on February 12th, 2027.

items.title: 5 Ways The Duskbloods’ Multiplayer Is Different From Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: The competitive multiplayer of The Duskbloods is a far cry from the collaborative matches of Nightreign, in more ways than players think.
items.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook The network test for The Duskbloods has started, showing just how different the game is from the other FromSoft multiplayer experience — Elden Ring Nightreign . Where Nightreign has up to three players collaborate to grow stronger and defeat Nightlord bosses, The Duskbloods introduces PvP elements instead. Although players can still team up together in the Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods has a variety of other features that are far different from what FromSoft fans are used to.

Multiplayer matches of The Duskbloods are called Dusk Battles, where players compete with each other throughout various Phases. Much like Nightreign , these matches see everyone roam around a large, semi open-world, gathering resources to get stronger while fighting basic enemies and roaming, randomly generated bosses. Players can either jump into matches solo in The Duskbloods , or team up with one other competitor in Duos, creating four teams of two who participate in the PvEvP battle royale style gameplay together.

Both The Duskbloods and Elden Ring Nightreign have playable characters that act as classes for players to choose from, each with their own play style, weapons, and abilities. In The Duskbloods , this manifests through six different Bloodsworn characters, with 10 planned “classes” for the game’s official launch and this reduced number for the network test. Every Bloodsworn in The Duskbloods is unique in their own way, having their own backgrounds and stories that emerge through gameplay in the same way as Nightreign .

However, the biggest difference between each FromSoft game is how the Bloodsworn of The Duskbloods don’t have builds entirely reliant on their own skills. Every character in The Duskbloods has two Bloodsworn abilities and multiple Aspects players can choose from for new passive effects, similar to the Relic items you can equip to characters in Nightreign . Yet, there are only a few Aspects to each Bloodsworn, with the rest of their build being determined by an external character you pick to fight alongside you. These allies, called Kin, can cover a Bloodsworn’s weaknesses depending on who you choose.

The network test has eight different Kin you can pair with your Bloodsworn for varied builds, with no ally character being restricted based on who you choose. Kin can be summoned like Spirit Ashes from Elden Ring , acting as separate but united characters who stay by your side until the end of a match. Some Kin provide passive buffs to your character, while others simply act as another fighter to distract bosses. Kin level up, but you can swap them out during a match at various portals that appear randomly on the map. Some of the Kin available include:

Much like how characters aren’t defined in a solo setting like they are in Nightreign , the in-game resources players earn during a match in The Duskbloods are also not as straightforward. Elden Ring had Runes that fueled your character being able to level up or buy new items, but The Duskbloods has a resource called Virtue. Every Dusk Battle requires you to build up Virtue through various tasks, with the players who earn the highest amount of Virtue moving on to other Phases of a Dusk Battle while others are eliminated.

You need to accumulate as much Virtue as possible to win a Dusk Battle, but there are several types of Virtue rather than it just existing as one type of currency. In fact, there are at least a half-dozen different kinds of Virtue, each gained in a different way for accomplishing certain tasks. To understand the basic types of Virtue in The Duskbloods , check out this breakdown:

There are other opportunities to earn Virtue, such as completing unique Events that take place throughout a Dusk Battle. For example, players might encounter an event where they are teleported to a bell tower, and are asked to ring the bell in that location to gain extra Virtue. While Nightreign is more concerned about you spending a match’s duration to strengthen your character, The Duskbloods ‘ progression is entirely tied to focusing on gathering as many types of Virtue as you can before Phases change.

In Elden Ring Nightreign , players go through three “Nights” throughout a run, with the match failing to progress if they don’t beat a particular boss on each Night. This structure is reflected somewhat by the four Phases that make up The Duskbloods , with the Switch 2 game also breaking up its exploration for mandatory gatherings of all players before opening the map back up again. Yet, these Phases are intense in a completely different way than Nightreign ‘s Nights, as they act as places where PvP creates chaotic clashes.

As each character in The Duskbloods earns Virtue, some will stand out over others. In between Phases, though, each player has a chance to make up for not having as much Virtue by taking it away from other competitors. The first Phase requires players to reach a specific quota of Virtue before they can move on, with three players being “culled” before Phase 2 begins. Between Phases 2 and 3, two more players are eliminated, before the remaining four enter Phase 4 together.

Phase 4 is not a place where you explore and gather more Virtue, but rather acts as a free-for-all where the last four players standing must eliminate each other to claim victory. During this Phase, players each have two lives they can burn through before being defeated, and must fight others in a PvP arena until one player is left standing. The last arena varies in The Duskbloods , sometimes with places you can fall from or enclosed walls that make the end of each Dusk Battle a chaotic and desperate affair.

In Nightreign , you are bonded to whatever players you are facing the Night with, as 1-3 players can embark on runs together without any sort of PvP. The Duskbloods is the opposite of this, as you are in competition with others the moment a Dusk Battle starts, but this doesn’t mean you can’t form temporary bonds with enemy players. You can initiate Alliances with another willing participant, during any Phase of a Dusk Battle other than the final one.

Players that choose to partner with each other can’t attack one another, and share rewards gained from various activities. This includes Virtue, meaning that players have better chances of growing their Virtue beyond other players that work alone. On the other hand, a player in an Alliance can call it off before Phase 4, gaining a penalty by “betraying” the person they allied with. This penalty includes surrendering a portion of your built-up Virtue, so you want to make sure to do this only if you’re confident it won’t affect your chances of being eliminated.

This system is great for struggling players with low Virtue to stave off the culling between Phases, at least until Phase 4 breaks any Alliance automatically to ensure a match only has one winner. However, the Duos mode of The Duskbloods makes Alliances permanent all the way until the end of any game, with teammates sharing lives in Phase 4 if they reach that stage. Instead of individual players getting eliminated each Phase, only one Team bites the dust, leaving the last two teams with the highest Virtue in Phase 4 to try and win.

items.title: Elden Ring-style RPG launches, free 3-hour prologue is a must-play this weekend
items.summary: Play the first three hours of Mortal Shell II before you buy.
items.content:
Mortal Shell 2 is out today, and you can play the first three hours for free.

You can play the first three hours of Mortal Shell II for free, giving Dark Souls and Elden Ring fans the chance to try the highly anticipated sequel to the acclaimed 2020 action RPG Mortal Shell before you buy.

When Mortal Shell launched in 2020, however, it’s fair to say that it didn’t completely blow the soulslike community away.

The game developed a dedicated following and proved to be a commercial success, selling more than one million copies worldwide within three years of launch. Critically, however, it was received as a solid but somewhat uneven soulslike rather than a genre-defining classic, earning a 76 critic score and 6.2 user score on Metacritic .

Six years have passed since the launch of the original game, and Mortal Shell II is now available across multiple platforms. In June 2026, a playable beta went live that allowed you to play the first three hours, essentially a prologue. That prologue is still available at launch, which is basically an extended demo.

The Mortal Shell II beta/demo is available on PC via Steam , PlayStation Store and the Xbox Marketplace .

Sort of. Your actual save data won’t carry over into the full game. But when you boot up Mortal Shell II , you will be given the option to skip the prologue. What’s more, for completing the demo/prologue, players will be rewarded with the ‘The Flayed Harbinger’ cosmetic outfit.

READ MORE: Elden Ring player discovers hidden item four years after launch

Mortal Shell II has not only vastly improved in the visuals department, but the developers have heavily focused on improving the combat, exploration, character class build options, weapon customisation and more. It also looks to have faster-paced action, which perhaps separates it from Dark Souls comparisons.

Moreover, at the time of writing, its Metacritic score currently sits at 8.4, an improvement on the original score of 7.7. On Steam, it’s rated as “ Very Positive ” from over 1,700 user reviews.

“This game lets you possess a seven-foot armoured muscle mommy to steamroll enemies without stamina management holding you back. Absolute peak soulslike, 10/10,” wrote Steam user MobiusBlack.

“The game is a clear evolution from the first one; combat is much better, and the movement doesn’t feel sluggish,” explained Jessica.

“The only downside is that regular enemies deal way more damage than necessary, to the point where it’s comparable to boss damage, which creates a very artificial difficulty for the game. I also can’t leave out the best part of the game, which made me a little jealous: Proxima’s design. She got cake.”

“ Mortal Shell II is a standalone sequel to Mortal Shell that significantly expands on the original with unrestricted, adrenaline-charged combat, extensive weapon upgrades, and free exploration,” reads the synopsis of the game.

Many fans were surprised when FromSoftware announced its PvPvE action game, The Duskbloods, so soon after releasing its multiplayer, roguelike Elden Ring spin-off, Nightreign .

However, according to game director Miyazaki, who also helmed Elden Ring , Bloodborne , and Dark Souls , releasing two multiplayer games back-to-back wasn't intentional.

"It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games would both release next to each other," Miyazaki told IGN , explaining that since Nightreign was led by a different director, Junya Ishizaki, both ideas "just coincided with being multiplayer games."

"It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward," Miyazaki continued. "We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."

Hold out for a little longer FromSoft fans — The Duskbloods will get a closed network test this summer, but a release date for the full game has yet to be announced The Duskbloods network test has finally revealed a few new details about FromSoftware's upcoming Switch 2 game, including multiplayer matches with 'up to eight players' 'Clair Obscur showed that you can take a genre and do it in a different and interesting way' — The Blood of Dawnwalker director says the ambitious game was made out of a 'love for RPGs' The director then suggested the studio could dive back into making single-player games after The Duskbloods arrives, saying: "But it's like, the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time, if anything, it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."

The studio's last single-player experience was Elden Ring , which launched in 2022, followed by the multiplayer spin-off, Nighreign , in 2025.

Next up for FromSoftware is The Duskbloods , which was announced last year as a PvPvE and Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive. Network tests are underway, but a release date hasn't been set.

But given Elden Ring : Nightreign's success , and the fact that The Duskbloods is shaping up to be pretty solid— boo, Switch 2 exclusive, boo —it's a true statement.

You might be wondering, then, if the undisputed king of gritty singleplayer RPGs where you dodge roll sometimes has gone all live service on us. Not so, says president Hidetaka Miyazaki, the combo of Nightreign and Duskbloods is literally just a coincidence.

Speaking to IGN , Miyazaki says: "It's not necessarily some big reveal saying this is the direction we plan to go in moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did. It's funny, because there was never really any big plan that these two games would both release next to each other."

That's not to say FromSoftware hasn't been enjoying itself, though—Miyazaki seems enthused by the opportunity to break from the formula every once in a while: "Personally, it's very fun to make a multiplayer game like this. It's not something we've done a lot and we're looking forward to seeing players' reactions and getting feedback."

But that enthusiasm doesn't override his love for what FromSoftware is provably good at: Making you throw your controller because goddamn Promised Consort Radahn's lazers keep filling up the goddamn screen and how am I supposed to dodge that, this is bullcrap. Ahem.

I'm a decade-plus FromSoftware sicko, and these are my 5 takeaways from the first Duskbloods gameplay Surely FromSoftware has something brewing besides that Switch 2 exclusive, right? FromSoftware boss Hidetaka Miyazaki references 'yet to be announced' games while commenting on controversy at parent company Kadokawa "If anything, it's like the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again," Miyazaki concludes—which is great news for me, as I'm personally excited to get stuck into whatever the next Elden Ring is. Sekiro 2, maybe? A parry-loving cretin can only hope .

items.title: 'Elden Ring Meets Settlers of Catan' Revealed as Switch 2's Next Multiplayer Swing
items.summary: What is The Duskbloods? We explain FromSoftware's Elden Ring successor.
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Michael McWhertor Published Aug 20, 2026, 10:00 AM EDT Previews The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive is an odd but compelling mix of gameplay styles

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Jump links Jump Links OK, so what is The Duskbloods? How matches work in The Duskbloods Kith and kin (and zeppelins) Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap If you've played a FromSoftware " Soulslike " during the past decade and a half, you probably know what to expect from the developer's games: white-knuckle combat, challenging and grotesque monsters, and inventive online interactions with other players both friendly and adversarial. FromSoftware's next game, The Duskbloods , will feel familiar in that sense. In it, players take on the role of supernatural beings known as Bloodsworn who hunt grisly creatures. Players will do so with the aid — and interference — of other players in online play.

Unlike Dark Souls and Elden Ring , The Duskbloods focuses less on players charging forward against challenging odds, dying repeatedly, and charging forward again. It is instead a match-based multiplayer game in which eight players fight to earn victory points called Virtue, following multiple possible pathways to victory.

Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki says he hopes The Duskbloods ' game design leads to "unexpected drama."

FromSoftware has described The Duskbloods as a PvPvE game. That's accurate, in that there are player-versus-player moments, including each match's final contest. But much of the game can be played fighting against the environment, and rarely facing off against other players. During a hands-on gameplay preview at FromSoftware's headquarters in Tokyo, I focused as much as I could on the PvE aspects of The Duskbloods , slaying hordes of creatures, powering up my character, and collecting items from the environment.

My strategy was successful enough that I ultimately won five of the matches we played as a group. But some matches were a total bust, and the PvP-focused players were victorious.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo In The Duskbloods , players choose a prebuilt character called a Bloodsworn. The pre-built nature of the characters is similar to those of Elden Ring Nightreign . Each has a close-range melee weapon and a long-range attack, and all characters have unique special abilities and superpowers, some of which unlock over the course of a match.

Bloodsworn all share one thing in common: They're all good at jumping, making them capable of easily navigating the highly vertical environments of The Duskbloods ' maps. Characters can triple jump, air dash, and perform a Superman-like leap to scale buildings, hop onto bridges, or cross vast chasms.

Bloodsworn have another ability in common. They can "Howl" to stagger enemies, similar to the stunning effect of Bloodborne 's firearms. Bloodsworn can then "Drink Blood" from a staggered foe to refill their health and spellbind certain foes to make them temporary allies.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo In FromSoftware's upcoming network test for The Duskbloods , six Bloodsworn are playable. More are expected for the game's 2026 launch on Nintendo Switch 2. The current list of Bloodsworn includes easy-to-grasp characters like Albert, who fights with a sword, submachine gun, and whips of blood, and weirdos like Zork, a man in a metal diving suit who uses a length of undersea cable and a speargun to fight. Zork can also take off like a rocket ship, thanks to his built-in jetpack.

Players of past FromSoftware games will find some analogs in the Bloodsworn cast. Chakram user Trang Lanh fights like Nightreign 's Duchess, while Zork is a classic Dark Souls "fat roll" type of fighter. But FromSoftware clearly isn't afraid to get weird with the playable roster: One character unlocks the ability to transform into a hungry dinosaur as he levels up.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo Matches of The Duskbloods , known as Dusk Battles, require eight players, based on the network test build I played. Each match can be played solo or in duos, and matches last roughly 25-30 minutes. Players matchmake into a game and are transported to one of the game's maps. I played exclusively on Lawanro City, a Victorian city that features a handful of key landmarks: a giant clock tower, an underground sewer system, a large cathedral, and a shallow lake. Forests, caves, and bridges flesh out the map.

Players can choose which sector of the map they want to spawn into, both at the start of the game and after dying. There's little to no penalty for dying, though it takes you out of the game for a moment and other players may benefit from your death.

Once on the map, your mission is explicit: earn Virtue. These points are akin to victory points in tabletop games, as The Duskbloods ' design was directly influenced by games like The Settlers of Catan , in which players have multiple avenues to victory.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
items.content:
The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The ‘Tarnished’, long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on 28th August .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

An epic drama born from a myth created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

Create and build your own character In addition to customising the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armour, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
